content.jointProblem: Can trace-driven profiling, resource allocation and interruption-aware scheduling reduce GenovaMed’s short-read star-allele pipeline toward below EUR 3 per sample and under 90 minutes per 24-sample batch without changing clinical accuracy? The first experiment would profile representative batches and replay selected VM/resource configurations against the unchanged pipeline, testing whether the researcher’s cloud models transfer to this genomic workflow before considering spot execution.

rationale.text: Đukić has directly relevant methods for investigating the trade-off between cloud rental cost and job latency.

sources.quote: A threshold-based control policy is derived by value iteration over a finite horizon of T = 200 decision epochs, with per-step costs reflecting both VM rental fees and job latency penalties.

rationale.text: Her multi-resource scheduling work provides a basis for examining CPU, memory and network allocation once the actual pipeline bottlenecks are measured.

sources.quote: Multi-tenant cloud platforms require scheduling decisions that jointly allocate CPU, memory, and network bandwidth across competing tenant queues.

rationale.text: Her research addresses both preemptible batch computing and checkpointing overhead, relevant to evaluating rather than assuming savings from spot instances.

sources.quote: This paper models a batch-processing workload that uses a mix of on-demand and preemptible instances
Long-running scientific workflow tasks benefit from periodic checkpointing to limit recomputation after node failures, but frequent checkpointing imposes I/O overhead.

rationale.text: She has experience translating analytical cloud models into industry-facing capacity and scaling work.

sources.quote: providing analytical support for their auto-scaling module design.
She has also delivered two workshops on queuing-theoretic capacity planning for engineering staff at NTP Novi Sad tenant companies.

constraints.text: Benchmark the existing Python/Snakemake cloud workflow at its operational batch size and cadence; isolated task speedups are insufficient without end-to-end measurement.

sources.quote: We wrote the pipeline ourselves in Python using Snakemake
Our bioinformatics pipeline takes a batch of 24 samples from raw sequencing reads to a final star-allele call in roughly four to six hours.
We run two batches a day on weekdays

constraints.text: Evaluate cost and turnaround jointly against the company's desired thresholds; these are experimental targets, not guaranteed outcomes.

sources.quote: A good outcome would be getting compute cost below 3 EUR per sample and ideally cutting total run time to under 90 minutes

constraints.text: Preserve clinical accuracy and agree validation and change-control requirements within the accredited laboratory workflow before production deployment.

sources.quote: without touching the clinical accuracy of the calls.
Our laboratory is accredited under ISO 15189 and every report is reviewed by a clinical pharmacist before it leaves the building.

constraints.text: Scope implementation and experiments to the company's limited staff time and approximately EUR 8,000 annual discretionary R&D budget.

sources.quote: The two-person bioinformatics team and two senior molecular biologists can dedicate roughly two days per week each to a collaborative project
a small discretionary R&D budget of approximately 8,000 EUR per year.

constraints.text: Secure suitable operational traces and confirm permitted use of any retained clinical samples; the research group has limited access to production data.

sources.quote: her group has the analytical tools but limited access to large-scale production data.
a set of retained clinical samples held under ethics approval

constraints.text: Confirm researcher capacity before scheduling: the notes describe room for one new collaboration in a dated 2025–2026 context, not a confirmed current allocation.

sources.quote: She is on a reduced administrative load in 2025–2026 due to her role as project PI
would be able to take on one new collaboration without difficulty.

risks: The relevant publications use synthetic cloud workloads, simulations or non-genomic traces, not this short-read star-allele pipeline. Their reported improvements cannot be transferred directly; the first profiling-and-replay experiment must test model applicability and prediction error.
No genomic calling or clinical validation expertise is established in the researcher's supplied material. GenovaMed must retain responsibility for allele-call validation and clinical acceptance.
Alignment and calling are only suspected bottlenecks. Serial computation, storage I/O or tool-specific limits could make cloud scheduling insufficient to reach the cost and runtime targets.
Spot interruptions could increase recomputation, cost and turnaround; task restartability and checkpoint support in the actual tools remain unknown.
The cloud provider, instance configuration, billing boundaries and permissions for sharing genomic data or operational traces are unknown, so feasibility and achievable savings remain uncertain.
Current researcher availability and project timeline are unknown; the small company budget may constrain profiling instrumentation, repeated benchmarks and implementation.
questions: Can Đukić confirm current availability for a joint project, the proposed start date and the time her group can commit?
Which cloud provider, VM types, storage and regional settings are used, and does EUR 9 per sample include storage, data transfer, idle capacity and failed runs?
Can GenovaMed provide the Snakemake DAG, tool versions, resource settings, representative execution logs and billing records, and permit collection of per-step CPU, memory and I/O measurements?
What representative validation set and acceptance criteria will establish unchanged clinical accuracy, including difficult CYP2D6 calls, and who signs off changes under the quality system?
What ethics, privacy, access-control and data-location restrictions apply to samples, sequencing reads and traces? Can benchmarking remain within the company's approved environment?
Which workflow steps support safe retries or checkpointing, and what interruption rate and deadline-miss risk would be acceptable for spot instances?
What project deadline and budget allocation are available for cloud experiments and implementation, and are the runtime and cost targets measured per batch, per sample or across routine operation?
